 Judgment

The appeal is filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 17.06.2011 passed by the Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-IX Mudhol, in MVC No.932/2007 on the ground that the liability of the insurance company is only at Rs.6,000/- as per Sub-Section (2) (b) of Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'the M.V. Act').

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-IX Mudhol
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The liability of the insurance company is only Rs.6,000/- in respect of damages caused to third party property.
Therefore, the insurance company is liable to pay compensation of Rs.6,000/- and the owner has to pay the remaining compensation to the claimant.
Therefore, prays to modify the judgment and award in this regard.
2. Admittedly, as per Ex.R.1-insurance policy, the insurance policy is a package policy.
Under package policy, the insurance coverage is unlimited.

Section 147 of the M.V. Act, stipulates regarding compulsory coverage of NC: 2023:KHC-D:13266 insurance and therefore, where policy is issued under Section 147 of the M.V. Act, the liability of the insurance company is limited to the extent what is stated in Section 147.
Where the insurance policy is package policy covering risk comprehensibly, then the insurance company shall pay actual compensation determined by the tribunal.
The point involved in this case is no more Res integra.
Therefore, the tribunal is correct in holding the insurance company has to pay entire compensation award to the claimant.
Accordingly, the appeal filed by the insurance company is dismissed.
